name: Todaimae
tagline: Otemachi in 16 minutes and Tokyo in 17 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥90,000 to ¥100,000.
summary: The station is in Bunkyo City, where Tokyo Metro run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 16 minutes to Otemachi, 20 minutes to Shinjuku, 27 minutes to Shibuya and 31 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. The station stands 21.6 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 14.0 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 21.6 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 7.8 m to 21.8 m, a difference of 14.0 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of less than 0.5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 1 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is less than 0.5 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 22 clinics and 20 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 日本医科大学附属病院, about 7 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 慈愛病院, about 9 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Metro Namboku Line.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Namboku Line runs at 156% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 駒込→本駒込, which this station is not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥90,000 to ¥100,000 and 1K ¥100,000 to ¥110,000. 1LDK ¥180,000 to ¥190,000 and 2LDK ¥240,000 to ¥250,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is among the lowest in the 23 wards. a small projected flood depth and schools and parks within walking distance pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station holds it down. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Todaimae is ahead on the number of medical facilities and quiet.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Todaimae. Hakusan has the Toei Mita Line, a different set from Todaimae. To Otemachi, for instance, Hakusan is 6 minutes quicker. A one-room flat costs about ¥6,000 more at Hakusan. On quiet, Todaimae comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: rents are lower at Nezu, but Todaimae is ahead on the number of medical facilities and how easy the shopping is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Todaimae. Nezu has the Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line, a different set from Todaimae. To Otemachi, for instance, Nezu is 7 minutes quicker. A one-room flat costs about ¥10,000 less at Nezu. On how easy the shopping is, Todaimae comes out ahead.

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 12 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 5 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyo Metro Namboku Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are among the lowest in the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are heavily loaded in the morning.
